name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.isCompactOperator_map_of_singleton
title: Every operator in a singleton image is compact

content.display_title: Every operator in a singleton image is compact
content.one_sentence_role: Excludes a noncompact image by making one separating character take both zero and one on the same projection.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ represent the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations of $A$. Then $$\pi(a)\in\mathcal K(H)\qquad(a\in A).$$
content.assumptions: No simplicity or separability of $A$ is assumed. The argument uses faithfulness of $\pi$ on $A$, not faithfulness of its unital extension on the whole unitization.
content.conclusion: This proves the inclusion $\pi(A)\subseteq\mathcal K(H)$ for the specified representation.
content.proof_summary: Separate a noncompact self-adjoint image from the compact-preimage ideal in a maximal abelian subalgebra. Its character produces a rank-one projection which belongs to the ideal but has character value one.
proof_steps: Suppose $\pi(a)$ is noncompact. Write $$a=\operatorname{Re}a+i\operatorname{Im}a,\quad \operatorname{Re}a=(a+a^*)/2,\quad\operatorname{Im}a=(a-a^*)/(2i).$$ If both self-adjoint parts had compact images, their sum would too. Choose a self-adjoint part $b\in A$ with noncompact $\pi(b)$. Write $\widetilde A=\mathbb C\oplus A$, $\iota(x)=(0,x)$, $\chi_\infty(\lambda,x)=\lambda$, and $\widehat\pi(\lambda,x)=\lambda I+\pi(x)$. Apply [A maximal abelian subalgebra containing a self-adjoint element](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/MaximalAbelianContaining.lean#L53-L59) to the self-adjoint $\iota(b)$ in the unital $\widetilde A$, obtaining a maximal abelian unital $*$-subalgebra $D$ containing it. Such a $D$ is norm closed.

For the representation $\rho_D=\widehat\pi|_D$, form [The compact-preimage ideal](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CompactPreimage.lean#L28-L63) and use [Norm closedness of the compact-preimage ideal](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CompactPreimage.lean#L72-L92) to obtain the closed ideal $$J=\{d\in D:\widehat\pi(d)\text{ is compact}\}.$$ Commutativity makes it an ordinary ideal of the commutative $C^*$-algebra $D$. The element $\iota(b)\in D$ is outside $J$, since $\widehat\pi(\iota(b))=\pi(b)$. Apply [A character separating a closed ideal](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/ClosedIdealCharacter.lean#L20-L65) to $J,\iota(b)$: obtain one character $\chi$ with $\chi|_J=0$ and $\chi(\iota(b))\ne0$.

The scalar character vanishes at $\iota(b)$, so $\chi\ne\chi_\infty|_D$. The closedness of $D$ and the singleton assumptions allow [A unit eigenvector for a non-scalar character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CharacterEigenvector.lean#L85-L197) to give a unit vector $\eta\in H$ with $\widehat\pi(d)\eta=\chi(d)\eta$ for all $d\in D$. Apply [Preimages of all rank-one operators](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CompactRange.lean#L94-L105) to $\eta,\eta$, using separability of $H$, and obtain $p\in A$ with $$\pi(p)=\theta_{\eta,\eta},\qquad\theta_{\eta,\eta}(z)=\langle\eta,z\rangle\eta.$$

For $d\in D$, both $d$ and $d^*$ lie in $D$, so $$\widehat\pi(d)\eta=\chi(d)\eta,\qquad\widehat\pi(d)^*\eta=\overline{\chi(d)}\eta.$$ Fix any $z\in H$ and use the inner product linear in its second argument. The two products are $$\widehat\pi(d)\theta_{\eta,\eta}z=\langle\eta,z\rangle\widehat\pi(d)\eta=\chi(d)\langle\eta,z\rangle\eta,$$ and $$\begin{aligned}\theta_{\eta,\eta}\widehat\pi(d)z&=\langle\eta,\widehat\pi(d)z\rangle\eta\\&=\langle\widehat\pi(d)^*\eta,z\rangle\eta\\&=\chi(d)\langle\eta,z\rangle\eta.\end{aligned}$$ The last equality uses conjugate linearity in the first argument. Thus these operators commute.

Write the same $d$ as $(\lambda,x)$ with $x\in A$. Substituting $\widehat\pi(d)=\lambda I+\pi(x)$ and $\theta_{\eta,\eta}=\pi(p)$ in the commutation identity and cancelling the scalar terms gives $$\pi(xp)=\pi(x)\pi(p)=\pi(p)\pi(x)=\pi(px).$$ By [Faithfulness on the original algebra](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/Singleton.lean#L33-L94), the original $\pi$ is injective; hence $xp=px$. Consequently $$d\iota(p)=(0,\lambda p+xp)=(0,\lambda p+px)=\iota(p)d.$$ This holds for every $d\in D$, so [The commutant of a maximal abelian subalgebra](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/MaximalAbelian.lean#L115-L136) gives $\iota(p)\in D$. No injectivity of $\widehat\pi$ is used.

The represented operator of $\iota(p)\in D$ is $\pi(p)=\theta_{\eta,\eta}$, which is compact. Thus $\iota(p)\in J$ and $$\chi(\iota(p))=0.$$ On the other hand, the eigenvector equation for this very element gives $$\begin{aligned}\chi(\iota(p))\eta&=\widehat\pi(\iota(p))\eta\\&=\theta_{\eta,\eta}\eta=\langle\eta,\eta\rangle\eta=\eta.\end{aligned}$$ Since $\|\eta\|=1$, this implies $\chi(\iota(p))=1$, contradicting its value zero. The original noncompact image is therefore impossible.
